## The Power Formula

```{=latex}
\begin{notebox}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{center}
$\displaystyle \text{power} \;=\; \Phi\!\left( \frac{|\mu_t - \mu_c|\sqrt{N}}{2\sigma} \;-\; \Phi^{-1}\!\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right) \right)$
\end{center}
\vspace{0.1em}
\end{notebox}

\vspace{0.2em}

Read it as a subtraction: \textbf{what you expect} $-$ \textbf{what you need} $=$ how much room you have. Feed that
difference into the table.

\vspace{0.3em}

\begin{center}
\small
$\underbrace{\dfrac{|\mu_t - \mu_c|\sqrt{N}}{2\sigma}}_{\text{what you expect, in standard errors}} \qquad
 \underbrace{\Phi^{-1}\!\left(1-\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)}_{\text{the bar you must clear}} \qquad
 \underbrace{\text{their difference}}_{\text{look this up in the table}}$
\end{center}
```

## The Minimum Detectable Effect (MDE)

```{=latex}
\begin{notebox}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{center}
$\displaystyle \text{MDE} \;=\; \left(\Phi^{-1}\!\left(1-\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\right) + \Phi^{-1}(\text{target power})\right) \;\times\; \frac{2\sigma}{\sqrt{N}}$
\end{center}
\vspace{0.1em}
\end{notebox}

\vspace{0.2em}

The same equation, solved for the effect instead of for power. At $\alpha = 0.05$ and 80\% target power the
leading bracket is $1.96 + 0.84 = \mathbf{2.80}$.
```

## Notation

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{7pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.28}
\begin{tabular}{c>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.4cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{9.6cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Name} & \textbf{What it is} \\
\midrule
$N$              & Sample size          & Total subjects collected, across both arms. \\
$\mu_t$          & Treatment mean       & Average outcome under treatment. \\
$\mu_c$          & Control mean         & Average outcome under control. \\
$\mu_t - \mu_c$  & Effect size          & The true difference between the two means: the \textit{signal}. Abbreviated $\delta$ in code. \\
$\sigma$         & Standard deviation   & How much outcomes vary from one another: the \textit{noise}. \\
$\alpha$         & Significance level   & Type I error rate you tolerate --- claiming an effect when there is none. Sets the bar. \\
$\beta$          & Type II error rate   & Probability of missing an effect that is real. \\
power            & $1 - \beta$          & Probability of detecting an effect that is real. \\
$\Phi$           & Normal CDF           & Area to the \textit{left} of a $z$-score. This is what the table gives you. \\
$\Phi^{-1}$      & Inverse normal CDF   & Its inverse: hand it an area, it returns the $z$-score. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

```{=latex}
$\Phi^{-1}(0.95)$  & 1.645 & The bar, for a one-sided test at $\alpha = 0.05$ \\
$\Phi^{-1}(0.80)$  & \textcolor{statorange}{\textbf{0.84}}  & Target power of 80\%, inside the MDE formula \\
$\Phi^{-1}(0.90)$  & 1.282 & Target power of 90\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

## Reading the Table, Both Directions

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{8pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabular}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.3cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5.6cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{6.6cm}}
\toprule
& \textbf{Forwards:} $z \rightarrow$ area \; ($\Phi$) & \textbf{Backwards:} area $\rightarrow z$ \; ($\Phi^{-1}$) \\
\midrule
You have    & A $z$-score, e.g. $0.28$ & An area, e.g. $0.975$ \\
You do      & Split it: $\mathbf{0.2}$ picks the row, $\mathbf{.08}$ picks the column & Hunt the area in the \textit{body} of the table \\
You read    & The cell where they meet & The row and column \textit{margins} of that cell \\
You get     & $\Phi(0.28) = .6103$, i.e. \textbf{power $= 0.61$} & Row $1.9$ + column $.06$, i.e. \textbf{$z = 1.96$} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3em}

\footnotesize The table below gives $\Phi(z)$ --- the area to the \textbf{left} of $z$ --- for $z \geq 0$.
For negative $z$, use $\Phi(-z) = 1 - \Phi(z)$.
```
